_note: EXTERIOR round 2, 2026-08-23. Room 11 'Frontyard' is not a room: it is the front of the house, and the only view it is ever seen from is the whole-house level ('all'), where the app hides generated room geometry and shows the shell GLB instead. SHOOT WITH --level all, NEVER --level 1: a level-1 shot drops into single-floor mode, which hides the shell, the lawn and the trees and shows a studio backdrop. Build scripts: scratchpad/ext/ (kit.py shared helpers, f_porch.py this room, b_deck.py + b_furn.py room 3, probe.py pixel->world raycast, scan.py / hmap.py shell-terrain scanners, meas.py metering). Most of this yard is NOT placed objects - it is procedural geometry in frontend/js/environment.js (addGroundCover + addFrontYard + addStreet), which is the right home for anything that has to be visible on the whole-house view and costs no GLB payload.

_environment_js._note: The bulk of the front yard is procedural. Round 2 re-authored the ground layer, the planting layout and the lot edge.
_environment_js.lawn: REWRITTEN. makeGrassTexture() was a white plate with 33% coverage of 1.5 px dots - relative sd 8%, rendering 3.4%, against the photograph's 8-15%. Now a full-coverage tile: per-texel GRAIN 50 + a 0.7 ft CLUMP octave 13 on mean 194, anisotropy 8. The tile carries NO low-frequency content on purpose - a first attempt with mower stripes and a 2.9 ft octave rendered the whole lawn as a visible 8.6 ft PLAID. Large-scale variation instead comes from a non-repeating world-space vertex tint (three octaves at 54/19/7 ft) written into the merged lawn mesh in buildYard. GRASS_BASE 0x53703c -> 0x67716a, solved by inverting the render's measured response, not picked by eye.
_environment_js.lawn_subdivision_bug: slab()'s segment arguments default to 1, so addGroundCover was laying every lawn patch as ONE QUAD - the entire yard's lawn merged to 30 triangles. Harmless while the lawn was flat colour, fatal the moment the tint went into vertex colours. Now subdivided at ~3.5 ft (5,670 tris).
_environment_js.ground_cover: One BASE SHEET at the low grade covering the whole site pad and 45 ft past it (it is also the only lawn geometry with enough vertices to carry the tint). Round 1 patched the pad region by region and left slivers of the GLB's pale slab showing wherever a patch stopped short; all of those rendered as thin WHITE LINES and read as leftover fence rails.
_environment_js.driveway: poured slab x 20.0..47.1 (west edge moved from 20.8 - see site_pad note), z 29.5..67.8, one longitudinal control joint and transverse joints every 12.5 ft. The CONCRETE ITSELF IS UNCHANGED: round 2's critic passed it and said leave it alone.
_environment_js.lot_edge: NEW - addStreet(). Sidewalk (4.4 ft, set back 7.6 ft from the kerb, with a grass verge), concrete curb broken at the drive, asphalt carriageway with a dashed centre line, a flared driveway apron, and a mailbox. Heights are tight: the 1200 ft grass disc sits at y -0.05 and the shell pad at 0.16, so the carriageway cannot be sunk below the lawn - it goes at y 0.00 and the curb does the reading.
_environment_js.west_planting: ONE CONTINUOUS SWEEP. Round 1 had a rectangle with a straight dark edge board plus a DETACHED island bed with a lamp post stranded in open lawn at x 10.4-20.5, z 52.8-63.3. Now the front bed runs from the porch's west return round the raised pad and down the whole west edge of the drive to the street, in three overlapping runs so the outer line steps in, with ONE scalloped dry-stacked stone edge tracing it.
_environment_js.east_planting: rock border the full length of the drive with the salvia mass, a small tree, four path lights, and the LAMP-POST bed at the street end - between the drive and the sidewalk, which is where 'Front of the house, a little bit of the garage and car pointing to a different house.jpg' actually puts it (see _disagreements).
_environment_js.beds: addBed density 0.5 -> 7.0 cobbles/sq ft and the stones are SMALLER (r 0.075-0.475 against round 1's 0.20-0.48). Octahedra below r 0.24 - at 4-8 screen px an 8-triangle blob and a 20-triangle one are the same picture, and there are ~6,700 stones across both yards. Cool blue-grey hue (photo meters B > G > R), value span 0.145-0.545, plus a coarse rim of larger pale stones where the rock meets lawn. The straight dark edge board is GONE.
_environment_js.stone_edging: NEW addStoneEdge() - dry-stacked scalloped slate along a world polyline, two staggered courses, each stone tilted, GREY (a first pass at hue 0.08 rendered as a brown timber edging board, i.e. the exact defect being fixed).
_environment_js.species: addBoxwood takes a species now: boxwood / euonymus / juniper / yew, each with its own hue, squash and spread. Round 1 was nine identical boxwood balls.
_environment_js.geese: two cast-concrete geese west of the porch steps ('Front of the house.jpg' x 660-590 y 875-900)
_environment_js.trees: addShadeTree unchanged. NO CONIFERS in the front half of the lot now (z > -8): round 1 stood one in the middle of the front lawn and it appears in no front photograph.
_environment_js.neighbours: addNeighbour rebuilt - 38-degree gable (was 20), eave overhang, fascia band, window openings, and its own MATTE bucket. Round 1 merged it into `beds`, whose UVs come from world X/Z, so every vertical face sampled one line of the grit tile and smeared it eave to grade. It also had an hsl() aliasing bug (hsl() returns the shared _c, so `wall` and `roof` were the same object) which is why it rendered as one flat grey mass. Two more houses added across the street.

driveway.verdict: unchanged authoring - the critic passed it and asked for it to be left alone. Sampled from a different box than round 1's, which is why |dx| reads lower here than round 1's reported 4.71.

_disagreements_with_the_round_2_critic: 'The front door is a black void with no leaf and no sidelights' is WRONG. The shell GLB models a six-panel dark door, white-cased sidelights with blue glass, and two coach lamps. See scratchpad/shots/v3_ext/r2_front_porch.png. The wreath WAS green and is now the photographed dark-red starburst; nothing else at that opening needed building.

'A detached island bed with a lamp post exists in no photograph' is WRONG about existence and RIGHT about siting. 'Front of the house, a little bit of the garage and car pointing to a different house.jpg' shows the lamp post plainly - a black lantern on a slim post standing in a sheet of green groundcover with ornamental grasses, edged in river rock, near the street. What was wrong was that round 1 put it in open lawn WEST of the drive; the photograph puts it EAST of the drive between the drive and the sidewalk, which is where it is now.

'The white 6-inch border band around the driveway slab' is not an outline we drew: probed (scratchpad/ext/probe.py) it is Root_Node - the shell's own pale driveway strip - at y 0.16, x 20.0-20.8, z 54-76, showing through because our concrete started at 20.8 and our lawn patch stopped at z 54.4. Fixed by covering, not by deleting anything.
_open: The shell GLB has a Sketchup SCALE FIGURE baked into its merged Root_Node mesh at about x -16.5, z 44.7. The west framing tree is deliberately planted over it. A SHELL_CUTS box would remove it.
Beds are still composed of rectangles; environment.js has no polygon bed primitive. The scalloped stone edge polyline is what gives the sweep its curve.

The yard's merged geometry is now 157,861 triangles across 8 meshes (beds 87,790 - mostly cobbles; leaves 58,687; lawn 5,670). That is up from ~75k and it is the price of the cobble field. One draw call each.
The exterior sky renders as a dull blue-grey even with --day; the photographs are bright. That is the app's daylight/weather, not this yard.
